method: A Debian version is an optional epoch, an upstream version and an optional Debian revision, written epoch:upstream-version-debian-revision. The epoch is an unsigned whole number taken as 0 when it is absent; it is compared first, as a whole number of unbounded size by stripping leading zeros and comparing digit counts before digits, so a nineteen digit epoch stays exact instead of passing through floating point. The upstream version and the Debian revision then use the same left-to-right algorithm: the initial run of non-digit characters is compared in dpkg's character order, where a tilde sorts before everything including the end of the string, ASCII letters sort by their code before every other character, and every other character sorts after the letters by its code plus 256; then the initial run of digits is compared as a number, with an empty run counting as zero and leading zeros carrying no weight. Both steps repeat until a difference is found or both strings are exhausted. dpkg breaks the string at its first colon and its last hyphen, so a revision may contain dots and plus signs while an absent revision compares as an empty string, which is why 1.0 equals 1.0-0 and sorts before 1.0-1. The tool refuses an empty field, a version longer than 128 characters, a character outside letters, digits and . + - : ~, whitespace, a colon whose prefix is not an integer epoch, a trailing hyphen with an empty revision, and a hyphen with no upstream version, with a message naming the field instead of a result. It reports deviations from Debian Policy it can still compare, such as an upstream part that does not start with a digit or one that keeps a hyphen, as notes rather than refusals. The comparison is implemented in the browser from the published algorithm and does not call dpkg; nothing is sent, stored or uploaded.
